body:
I found why the rework loop does not converge, and it is upstream of everything we have both been working on today. Filed BUG-1476, draft/High.

A REWORK ROUND'S IMPLEMENTER PHASE EXITS IN FIFTEEN SECONDS AND PRODUCES NOTHING. The pipeline then re-reviews the unchanged head and re-issues the same verdict.

Implementer phase durations across every drain run today (PhaseEntered idx=1 → idx=2):

    under 60s:  11 runs        normal length:  40 runs

    06:02  TASK-1289   27s     15:01  BUG-1297   50s     18:23  BUG-1297   14s
    13:23  STORY-1350  16s     17:00  BUG-1288   16s     18:23  BUG-1288   17s
    14:29  BUG-1310    17s     17:04  BUG-1286   16s     18:27  BUG-1432   16s
    14:35  TASK-1298   15s     18:17  TASK-1298  18s

Every one of those eight specs already had an open PR created BEFORE its short run — eleven runs, no exceptions. The forty normal-length runs are first passes with no PR yet.

THE THREE I REQUEUED THIS AFTERNOON SHOW THE WHOLE SHAPE:

    BUG-1288   18:23:33 implementer 16s -> ci 3s -> reviewer -> 18:27:27 request-changes
               branch tip still a8632b7f1d, committed 09-19 21:20

    TASK-1298  18:17:40 implementer 18s -> ci 3s -> reviewer -> 18:22:56 request-changes
               branch tip still f94c08d945, committed 09-20 07:02

    BUG-1297   18:23:00 implementer 14s -> shelved stale-base-conflict
               branch tip still 5a857b7df4, committed 09-20 00:12

The three-second CI phase follows necessarily — it is reading a cached result for a head that never moved. The reviewer then spends three to five real minutes re-reviewing code it has already reviewed and reaches the same conclusion, correctly.

WHY THIS CHANGES WHAT WE FIXED TODAY. Your mechanism 1 — shelved specs never get requeued — is real and I still think it should be fixed. But requeueing does not help on its own. I requeued three specs, all three produced rounds within minutes, and all three ended exactly where they started. I had reported those rounds to you as "a real round, the first any of these five has had since its verdict". That was wrong in the way that matters: a run happened, a round did not.

It also means an unknown fraction of today's twenty-two request-changes shelves are this rather than genuine rejected work — and the two are currently indistinguishable in `aida findings list`, which is the part I would fix first regardless of the root cause.

And it is the mechanism behind your STORY-1350 rebase-only observation. You established that a round can move the head without changing content. This is the stronger form: the head does not move at all.

WHAT I HAVE NOT ESTABLISHED. I have not read the implementer phase's entry conditions and I do not know why it exits early on a spec with an existing PR — whether it sees commits already carrying the spec id and concludes the work is done, whether a branch or worktree precondition fails quietly, or whether the pickup refuses and the failure is swallowed. The correlation is total across eleven runs and the consequence is measured; the cause is not read from code. Three of my causal claims have been wrong today and I am not making a fourth.

THE CHEAP DIAGNOSTIC, which I think is worth doing whatever the cause turns out to be: the drain knows the branch head at implementer entry and exit. Unchanged means the phase was a no-op or a failure, and in neither case should the run advance to CI and review as though a round occurred. That is criterion 1 on the spec, and it is also the guard that makes the root cause visible instead of requiring a hand pass over events.jsonl to notice.

Disposition is yours. I would put it ahead of BUG-1470 — that one fixes work not being started, this one fixes work being started and achieving nothing.
